about: All 55 trophies with their official PlayStation names, descriptions and grades. Guides are original to this entry and cite their sources beside each trophy. Missable flags and the roadmap order are derived from the official descriptions.

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: The platinum is awarded automatically the moment the other 54 trophies are all earned, so there is nothing separate to hunt: work the roadmap stage by stage and keep an eye on the missable flags in stages 2 and 3, because a missed one-off moment is the only thing that can force a second playthrough. Your last unlocks will almost certainly be A Long Road (100% completion) and one of the big counters, so check the tracker before the finale and sweep what is left.

sources.name: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PS5)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: Gone Fishing is the opening mission of the campaign, so this unlocks simply by playing the first minutes of the story and finishing the introductory job. It cannot be missed: the campaign cannot advance past it, and the chapter trophies that follow all build on this start.

sources.name: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PS5)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Finish every mission that makes up Chapter 1 of the story, starting with Gone Fishing. Chapter trophies are structural — the next chapter only opens when the current one is done — so this is earned on any full story playthrough with no detours required.

sources.name: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PS5)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: Play through Chapter 2 to its final mission. The chapter is a mandatory block of the campaign, so the trophy is unmissable on a story run; the name is printed exactly as PlayStation publishes it, asterisks included.

sources.name: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PS5)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: Complete the missions of Chapter 3. Like the other chapter trophies this one is locked to story progression and cannot be skipped or failed permanently — finish the chapter and it pops at the chapter break.

sources.name: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PS5)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 4, the last full chapter before the endgame. It is a required part of the campaign, so any player who reaches the final mission has already earned it; no side content is needed.

sources.name: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PS5)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: Beat the campaign's final mission after Chapter 4. Before you start it, sweep the flagged one-off trophies in this roadmap (Actions Speak Louder, Bad Luck, I Guess and Personal Best sit in the same endgame stretch): the finale is the point of no return for anything tied to story choices, while free-roam content stays open afterwards for the 100% push.

sources.name: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PS5)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: Breakfast Run is one of the named story missions, and this trophy is its completion stamp. Play the campaign in order and it unlocks when the mission ends; named-mission trophies like this one double as a checklist of how far through the story you are.

sources.name: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PS5)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: Finish the story mission The Cartel Heist. It is a set-piece heist inside the campaign rather than one of the repeatable free-roam robberies, so it is earned by story progression alone — follow the mission markers through the chapters and it will be offered as part of the plot.

sources.name: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PS5)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Child's Play when it appears in the campaign sequence. As with the other named-mission trophies there is no extra condition beyond finishing the mission, and it cannot be bypassed on the way to the finale.

sources.name: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PS5)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: Finish the story mission Headliners. It sits in the named-mission run of the campaign (Breakfast Run, The Cartel Heist, Child's Play, Headliners, VCIA Takedown, Operation Savage Glory), and completing it in the story earns the trophy with no optional objectives attached.

sources.name: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PS5)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: Complete VCIA Takedown, the story mission set around Vice City International Airport (VCIA). While you are at the airport for this mission, note the separate feat trophy Catch Me If You Can, which also happens at VCIA and is flagged missable in this guide — do it in the same visit if the opportunity appears.

sources.name: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PS5)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide: Finish Operation Savage Glory, the last of the named story missions before the endgame. Completion in the campaign is the whole requirement; after this one, only the final mission stands between you and the gold story trophy.

sources.name: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PS5)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: Reach a full 100% on the game's completion counter. In this series the counter is a weighted checklist — story missions, stranger strands, collectibles, activities and exploration all feed it — so the practical route is to finish everything else in this guide first and then use the in-game completion screen to find the last missing items. It is deliberately placed in the final roadmap stage: almost every other trophy is a down payment on it.

sources.name: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PS5)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Complete 250 of the stunt jumps scattered across Leonida. Work them region by region whenever you pass a ramp rather than saving them all for the end, and use a fast, durable vehicle you can replace cheaply — failed landings do not count, only clean completed stunts do. The counter is large but every stunt stays available, so nothing here can be missed.

sources.name: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PS5)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Sample every activity type the game offers at least once: races, drone races, the shooting range, fishing, arcade games, meditation spots and the rest of the map's activity icons. You only need to start each type, not win it, so a single free-roam session touring the icons earns this — and it doubles as a tour of what the other activity trophies will ask you to master.

sources.name: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PS5)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Gold-medal every Shooting Range challenge — the published list tracks 42 of them across the ranges of Leonida. Learn one range's target patterns at a time and replay immediately while the layout is fresh; accuracy medals usually reward a slower, fully-aimed run over a fast spray. Challenges can be retried without limit, so this is a skill gate, never a missable.

sources.name: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PS5)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win the Top Fun drone race at each of its locations around the map — a win at every site is required, not just a finish. Run a sighting lap first to learn each course's gates, then race it properly; the courses stay available all game, so clear them city by city as you explore.

sources.name: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PS5)
Rockstar Games — Grand Theft Auto VI

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Win 20 different races — repeat wins on the same track do not add to the count, so keep moving to fresh race icons. Start with the shortest street races to build the number quickly, and bring a tuned car you own rather than a borrowed one so the handling is predictable from race to race.

sources.name: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PS5)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Out-fish Cal in one of his fishing challenges. Fishing challenges are offered by Cal as a repeatable activity, so learn the cast-and-reel timing on a practice round first, then challenge him once you can land fish reliably. Losing costs nothing but time — challenge him again until you win.

sources.name: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PS5)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: Play one of the arcade cabinets found in Leonida's bars and arcades through to completion — finishing a single arcade game is enough, not beating every cabinet. Pick the shortest game on offer if several are available; this also ticks the arcade type off Master of None.

sources.name: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PS5)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Work Andy's stranger strand all the way to its final mission and finish it. Stranger strands unlock in stages as you meet each character and return later, so start Andy's strand early and check the map for his icon whenever a new mission appears — strands count toward the Strangers & Freaks total of eight as well as the 100% counter.

sources.name: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PS5)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Finish Kenton's stranger strand through its final mission. As with the other named strangers (Andy, Billy, Randy, Tyrone), the strand is a chain: each completed job unlocks the next after some in-game time passes, so if Kenton's icon vanishes, advance the story or sleep and it will return.

sources.name: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PS5)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Complete Billy's stranger strand to its final mission. Billy's jobs are one of the strands feeding Strangers & Freaks, so finish the whole chain rather than stopping at the first job; the trophy only pops on the strand's finale.

sources.name: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PS5)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Fully complete eight stranger mission strands anywhere in Leonida. The named strands with their own finale trophies — Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy and Tyrone — are five of the eight, so finish those first and then complete any three further strands you meet. A strand only counts when its final mission is done, so track chains, not first meetings.

sources.name: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PS5)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Finish Randy's stranger strand through its final mission. Keep the strand moving whenever Randy's icon is on the map — strand missions often gate the next step behind a delivery or a wait, and leaving them half-done is the usual reason this trophy feels stuck.

sources.name: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PS5)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Complete Tyrone's stranger strand to its final mission. Together with Andy, Kenton, Billy and Randy, Tyrone's strand is one of the five named strands; clearing all five leaves only three more strands needed for the silver Strangers & Freaks trophy.

sources.name: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PS5)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Visit every meditation spot in Leonida and meditate at each one. Treat the spots as a collectible set: sweep them county by county and tick them off in this tracker as you go, because the game gives no partial trophy — only the final spot triggers it. Meditation spots also count as an activity type for Master of None.

sources.name: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PS5)
Rockstar Games — Grand Theft Auto VI

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Take Bret's hunting job and bring down the unique animal he sends you after. Unique animals are one-off hunts tied to Bret's strand rather than the ordinary wildlife, so follow his lead to the hunting ground and track the specific animal he names; ordinary kills do not substitute.

sources.name: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PS5)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide: Assemble three complete sets of the collectible cards hidden around Leonida. Cards are found one at a time in the world, so grab every card you spot while doing other content and check the collection screen to see which sets are closest to done — finishing the three shortest sets is far quicker than completing the whole deck.

sources.name: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PS5)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide: Use the WAiNK It spot at 100 different locations. These spots behave like a collectible trail spread across the state, so work them into your travel routes and mark districts off in this tracker as you clear them; revisiting the same spot does not advance the counter, only new locations count.

sources.name: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PS5)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: Complete any 50 of the game's Challenges. Challenges are the short tracked objectives the game lists per activity and skill, so open the challenges screen, sort by the ones closest to completion, and mop those up first — most players cross 50 naturally by finishing the activity trophies in this roadmap.

sources.name: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PS5)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: While travelling with your partner (the other protagonist), raise a four-star wanted level and then lose it completely with them still beside you. Deliberately earn the stars somewhere with an easy escape — near tunnels, alleys or a vehicle swap — then break line of sight and stay hidden until the stars drain. It is repeatable in free roam, so a failed escape just means trying again.

sources.name: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PS5)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: With your partner alongside, rob three shops in one unbroken wanted sequence — the wanted level must never fully clear between shops. Pick a tight cluster of shops, keep a fast car outside each one, and move straight to the next target while the stars are still up; losing the heat or splitting up resets the chain.

sources.name: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PS5)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: Discover 100 different vehicles — a vehicle is discovered the first time you get in and drive it. Work through traffic variety deliberately: richer districts spawn sports cars, industrial areas spawn trucks and utility vehicles, and marinas and airfields cover boats and aircraft. Swap cars often instead of living in one favourite and the counter climbs fast.

sources.name: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PS5)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: During one activation of Combat Focus, drop five enemies before the effect ends. Set the moment up: trigger a fight against a grouped patrol or gang spot, line the enemies up first, then activate Focus and work left to right with a high-capacity weapon. If a run falls short, any crowded firefight gives you another attempt — nothing about it is one-time.

sources.name: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PS5)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: At VCIA (Vice City International Airport), take off in an aircraft outside any scheduled mission departure — steal a plane and get airborne from the airfield. Flagged missable from the description: the natural window is the VCIA Takedown story mission, when you are on the airfield with aircraft in reach; if you leave the airport section without doing it, you may not get the same scripted chance again, so do it during that mission first and try free-roam airfield access afterwards only as a backup.

sources.name: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PS5)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide: The description is a series in-joke: the Rhino is the tank. Get into a Rhino tank — they appear at military installations and at high wanted levels — and the trophy is tied to taking one for a spin. Expect heavy resistance stealing one from a base, so bring armour and an escape plan; once you are in the seat, you are the danger.

sources.name: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PS5)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store and get out without ever being detected — no alarm, no wanted level. Scout the store first, enter quietly, keep the staff controlled without firing a shot, and leave on foot to a discreet vehicle rather than screeching away. Jewelry stores can be robbed again, so a blown attempt only costs a retry.

sources.name: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PS5)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: Rob five bank vaults and escape the police after each one — a robbery only counts when you get away, not when you are caught or killed holding the money. Space the five out so you can bank the cash and reset between jobs, and stage a fast, plain car a block away from each bank for the getaway.

sources.name: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PS5)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Hold up an armored truck in free roam, take the cash and escape the wanted level. Armored trucks run delivery routes around the map; block one with a heavy vehicle, deal with the guards quickly, and break the rear doors rather than wasting time on the cab. One successful truck-and-escape is all it takes.

sources.name: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PS5)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide: Uncover the whole map of Leonida, the state Vice City sits in. Exploration registers by area, so the last few percent are always the far corners: island chains, swamp interiors and the northern border country. Finish the story first — some areas open up as the campaign expands — then do a deliberate border-to-border sweep by air to catch whatever is left fogged.

sources.name: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PS5)
Rockstar Games — Grand Theft Auto VI

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Hit an illegal operation owned by every gang in the game — one per gang, not the same gang repeatedly. Gang operations sit in gang territory, so learn each gang's turf from the map and your story progress, rob one operation in each, and expect the owning gang to defend it. Keep a list in this tracker: the trophy gives no partial credit until every gang has been hit.

sources.name: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PS5)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Have the cocktail-with-a-view moment at Ocean Beach, Vice City's beachfront strip. Flagged missable from the description: the name ('In The Beginning…') and the wording point to an early-game story beat rather than a repeatable free-roam action, so when the story takes you to Ocean Beach in the opening hours, take the moment instead of rushing the objective — if you play past it, a fresh save may be the only way back.

sources.name: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PS5)
Rockstar Games — Grand Theft Auto VI

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Inside a vehicle showroom, get into one of the display cars and drive it out through the showroom glass. 'In classic style' is the series' wink at driving straight through the window rather than using the door. Showrooms stay open in free roam, so if the first attempt ends in a wall, walk back in and take another car.

sources.name: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PS5)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Go to the Kolt & Associates bowling alley named in the description and bowl — 'follow-through' is the bowling motion, so play a game (or at least bowl your frames) at that specific alley rather than any other. The name is printed exactly as PlayStation publishes it, curly apostrophe included.

sources.name: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PS5)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.guide: The description is deliberately cryptic — a 'partnership with mass appeal' — and sits in the list among the endgame story-adjacent trophies, between the bowling feat and the choices trophy. Flagged missable on that reading: it most plausibly rewards a specific joint moment or outcome for the two protagonists' partnership late in the story, so keep both partners' joint activities and story beats completed as they appear, and do not rush the finale with partner content outstanding.

sources.name: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PS5)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.guide: This trophy is about the story's choices — 'for better or worse' in the description is the tell. Flagged missable: choice-driven trophies can depend on which option you pick at a branching moment, and the opposite branch closes behind you. Keep a manual save before major story decisions from Chapter 3 onward; if a choice resolves and no trophy pops, reload the save and take the other branch rather than playing on.

sources.name: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PS5)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.guide: 'Second time's the charm' implies a specific attempt that must fail (or be done a particular way) before it can succeed — a scripted retry moment rather than a counter. Flagged missable because such beats are usually welded to one story or strand mission: when a mission objective seems designed to go wrong the first time, let it, and take the second attempt the game offers instead of reloading a checkpoint to 'fix' the failure.

sources.name: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PS5)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.guide: The name and the baffled description mark this as the game's weird-event trophy — the series tradition of a strange encounter out in the wilds of the map. When something unexplained happens in rural Leonida (lights, a creature, a lone weirdo with a story), see it through to the end instead of driving on; one-off world events like this are found by exploring off-road areas, especially at night, and the event itself is the trophy.

sources.name: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PS5)
Rockstar Games — Grand Theft Auto VI

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: From a moving vehicle, knock down pedestrians with a melee drive-by — swinging a melee weapon from the car or bike as you pass. The bowling name suggests a group: line up a cluster of pedestrians on a pavement, ride past at moderate speed (too fast and you just run them over, which is a different animation), and sweep the whole group in one pass. Any busy pavement works and it is endlessly repeatable.

sources.name: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PS5)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Launder a cumulative $250,000 of Marked Bills through your contacts. Marked bills come from robberies and scores; instead of spending dirty cash as it arrives, route it through the laundering contacts whenever you are carrying some, and the total will accumulate across the whole playthrough. It pairs naturally with Maximum Withdrawal and the other robbery trophies in stage 7.

sources.name: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PS5)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Spend a cumulative $100,000 in shops — any shops, any goods: vehicles, weapons, clothes, services. There is no reason to grind this early; a full playthrough with car purchases and upgrades passes the total on its own. If you are short at the end, buying and upgrading one expensive vehicle closes the gap in a single transaction.

sources.name: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PS5)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: Buy every garage property on the map. Garages unlock for purchase as you progress and discover their districts, so this is partly an exploration trophy: finish The Goodtime State's map sweep, then visit each for-sale garage and buy it. Save the most expensive ones for after the story, when heist money has filled your account.

sources.name: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PS5)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register ten vehicles to the Scooter Bros app — the in-game service the description names. Registration is done per vehicle through the app, so each time you acquire a car or bike you intend to keep, register it on the spot rather than meaning to do it later; ten keepers accumulate quickly across a playthrough, especially while discovering vehicles for Whip It Good.

sources.name: Exophase — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies (PS5)
PSNProfiles — Grand Theft Auto VI trophies
